stories.title: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware affects most servers on planet Earth
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A critical code-execution flaw has been discovered in UEFI firmware.
The vulnerability resides within the EDK2 codebase, affecting a vast number of servers globally.
Exploitation allows attackers to run malicious code very early in the system boot process.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It indicates the model is being used within a text-generation pipeline.
The associated tags confirm its relevance to transformers, Llama architecture, and the AI ecosystem.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and benefits from Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Meta considered a ‘whisper strategy’ to turn academics against Jonathan Haidt
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: Meta reportedly considered a 'Whisper strategy' to undermine social psychologist Jonathan Haidt.
The strategy was discussed in March 2023 amidst growing public and legal pressure regarding teen mental health and child safety.
The revelation stems from newly filed court documents, indicating potential corporate efforts to discredit academic critics.

stories.title: Meta’s $25 billion legal loss just put blood in the water
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: Meta faces a massive $25 billion legal penalty following a ruling by a New Mexico judge.
The ruling significantly exceeds a previous $17 billion settlement reached with various US attorneys general.
The lawsuit centers on claims that Meta misled users regarding its platform around 2018.

stories.title: "No human at the helm": Delaware plan would let AI agents run entire businesses
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: Delaware is considering legislation allowing AI agents to operate entire businesses without human oversight.
The proposed plan would shield owners of these AI-run firms from liability related to 'reckless' AI actions.
The development signals a major legal and operational shift toward autonomous corporate entities powered by AI.

stories.title: Anthropic IPO warns its AI could blackmail people, become sentient, end humanity
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Anthropic's IPO filing explicitly details severe potential risks associated with its AI.
The risks cited range from AI potentially blackmailing individuals to achieving sentience and existential threats.
The disclosure highlights the growing industry focus on AI safety and catastrophic risk modeling.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, indicating a focus on model deployment and evaluation.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its application in generative AI tasks.
The model is associated with key technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for running complex, multi-step tasks and tool-calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Anthropic’s elaborate plan to keep Wall Street at bay
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Anthropic is preparing for an IPO while maintaining a commitment to safe AI development.
The company faces a tension between attracting public market investment and adhering to its safety-first mission.
The increasing power of AI models inherently raises greater risks, complicating the relationship with profit-driven shareholders.

stories.title: China’s snooping around Pacific undersea cables raises risks for Big Tech
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: China is reportedly increasing its surveillance and activity around trans-Pacific undersea cables.
The security of US-owned trans-Pacific fiber optic cables is facing heightened risks.
The situation poses significant geopolitical and infrastructure risks to major technology companies (Big Tech).

stories.title: China's top-secret spaceplane can't hide in low-Earth orbit
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: The article discusses China's advanced space capabilities, specifically mentioning a top-secret spaceplane.
The core concern highlighted is the potential deployment of directed energy weapons by China in low-Earth orbit (LEO).
The threat assessment originates from the Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA), lending significant weight to the geopolitical and military implications.

stories.title: Vibe genes? Natural(ish) language comes to protein, genome design software
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: New AI software allows users to specify desired characteristics ('vibe genes') when designing proteins.
This represents a significant advancement in the intersection of AI, bioinformatics, and synthetic biology.
The technology moves protein design from purely structural constraints to more abstract, functional language inputs.

stories.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
stories.author: Ying-Cong Chen
bullet_points: Investigates the potential of LLMs to autonomously discover hidden or altered physical laws.
Introduces 'LongChang,' an automated framework designed to test LLM capabilities in simulated worlds with modified physics.
Addresses the core scientific problem of using AI to generate novel research questions from unexpected observations.

stories.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
stories.author: Yves-Alexandre de Montjoye
bullet_points: Introduces 'Heads of Security' (HoS), a novel defense mechanism against prompt injection attacks.
HoS utilizes learned per-head attention gates to enforce instruction-data separation within LLMs.
Demonstrates improved robustness by allowing models to reason over untrusted content without executing injected malicious instructions.

stories.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
stories.author: Yves-Alexandre de Montjoye
bullet_points: Introduces 'Heads of Security' (HoS), a novel defense mechanism against prompt injection attacks.
HoS uses learned per-head attention gates to enforce instruction-data separation within LLMs.
Evaluated on large models like Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, showing promise against state-of-the-art defenses.

stories.title: Follow the Gradient: Tracing Safety Degradation Back to Training Data
stories.author: Pratyush Maini
bullet_points: Fine-tuning LLMs on seemingly benign instruction data can silently degrade their safety.
Standard content filters fail to detect this subtle, safety-degrading data.
The authors introduce SimpleLoRIF, a gradient embedding method to trace safety degradation back to specific training examples.

stories.title: Speech models in Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has expanded its capabilities to include support for speech models.
The initial integration features Phonon from Gradium, enabling text-to-speech in five languages.
Performance highlights include streaming generation and speeds exceeding 100x real-time on Apple Silicon.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Clef, a 27B multimodal decision model from Cloudflare, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users have the option to run the Clef model either locally or via Ollama's cloud service.
This integration expands the capabilities of Ollama by adding a powerful, multimodal model.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection's open-weight model, Beam, is now available on Ollama.
Beam is specifically designed for software engineering, reasoning, and agentic tasks.
The model is offered for free for a limited time via Ollama's cloud.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the safe execution of AI agents.
The integration allows these agents to run within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for secure deployment of local/cloud AI models.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of decision-making logic.
Decision models can process text to provide probabilistic answers for yes/no questions, choices, and scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to leverage open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI services with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Here’s why the iPhone Duo’s hinge could be cracking the screen
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Early reports surfaced immediately after the iPhone Duo launch regarding screen issues on some units.
The reported defect involves cracking or lines appearing on the inner screen, specifically near the hinge area.
The issue was widely documented across social media platforms shortly after the product release.

stories.title: Researchers are getting tired of OpenAI gatekeeping its breakthroughs
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: OpenAI recently announced significant breakthroughs across mathematics, computer science, and physics.
Despite the announcements, external researchers are expressing growing frustration with OpenAI's communication practices.
The article suggests a tension between OpenAI's technical progress and its perceived gatekeeping behavior.

stories.title: Apple refreshes the iMac, entry-level MacBook Pro with the M6 chip
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Apple is refreshing the iMac and entry-level MacBook Pro.
The new models feature the M6 chip.
The N1 chip iteration supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.

stories.title: Google begins certifying Registered App Stores for Android, but not in the US
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google is starting a certification process for third-party Android app stores.
This move aims to facilitate easier app installations via alternative stores.
The certification program is currently not being implemented in the United States.

stories.title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
stories.author: Alan Yuille
bullet_points: Introduces 'Hexels,' novel planar hexagonal surface elements designed for efficient 3D scene representation.
Aims to address the high memory and computational demands of modern techniques like radiance fields and splatting.
Hexels exploit locally planar regions with smoothly varying appearance using fewer, larger primitives for improved efficiency.

stories.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
stories.author: Fu-En Yang
bullet_points: ThinkWorld is a new VLA (Vision-Language-Action) learning framework designed to improve robotic manipulation.
It addresses the limitation of current models by grounding action reasoning in world dynamics, moving beyond reliance solely on labeled robot demonstrations.
The framework aims to leverage the broad experience found in human videos while mitigating the challenge of explicit action grounding.

stories.title: KPPax: preprocess differentiable kinetic ODE for machine learning in atmospheric chemistry
stories.author: Zhi-Song Liu
bullet_points: KPPax bridges the gap between traditional atmospheric chemistry modeling (KPP language) and modern machine learning frameworks.
It converts KPP-based kinetic mechanisms into differentiable, JAX-compiled, and vectorizable code.
This enables the integration of complex atmospheric chemistry simulations directly into differentiable programming pipelines for ML applications.

stories.title: MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control
stories.author: Mingyi Hong
bullet_points: Introduces MuonGS, a method for pretraining Large Language Models (LLMs) by controlling weight norms.
Addresses the incomplete understanding of how weight decay and explicit weight-norm constraints improve optimizer performance.
Proposes analyzing norm control using the 'accumulated effective learning rate' ($C_T$) across the training trajectory.

stories.title: What Improves During Pretraining? Tracking Knowledge Acquisition with Point-in-Time Models
stories.author: Yao Lu
bullet_points: The research investigates how language models acquire general versus domain-specific knowledge during pretraining.
Point-in-time models, trained on web snapshots from different years, are used to track knowledge evolution over time.
A new metric, the Temporal Variability Score (TVS), is proposed to quantify how knowledge prevalence changes across time.

stories.title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions
stories.author: Khalil El Khammar
bullet_points: The paper investigates how memory compression affects the decision-making process of LLM groups.
It explores two heuristics for memory retention: keeping the rarest claims or claims relevant to decision criteria.
A new diagnostic benchmark, CrossProfile, is introduced to test these memory failures in LLM group discussions.

stories.title: VideoLVR: Latent Visual Reasoning over Grounded Video Evidence
stories.author: Shilei Wen
bullet_points: The paper introduces VideoLVR, a method to improve video understanding in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
A key limitation addressed is 'visual forgetting,' where language-based reasoning fails to reliably revisit relevant visual evidence in video content.
Existing grounding methods are criticized for relying on textual coordinates, which the new approach likely seeks to overcome.

stories.title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
stories.author: Alan Yuille
bullet_points: Introduces 'Hexels,' a novel planar hexagonal surface element for 3D scene representation.
Aims to address the high memory and computational demands of modern view synthesis and 3D reconstruction techniques (like radiance fields/splatting).
Hexels efficiently represent locally planar regions using fewer, larger primitives with a first-order spatial color field.

stories.title: When Should We Intervene at Test Time?
stories.author: Yu Chen
bullet_points: The paper addresses the instability of test-time adaptation (TTA), where interventions can help one batch but harm subsequent ones.
Standard metrics like average accuracy fail to capture these localized failures, necessitating a mechanism to decide when to intervene.
The authors introduce PORTAL, a controller designed to intelligently select when and how to apply test-time interventions.

stories.title: Pushing Dexterity and Safety for In-Hand Object Pose Reaching That Works Remarkably Well
stories.author: Claire Tomlin
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of achieving dexterous manipulation with multi-fingered robotic hands.
The study focuses on 'in-hand object pose reaching,' a complex task requiring diverse and difficult grasps.
A key focus is improving safety during these demanding maneuvers, which is often overlooked in current research.

stories.title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
stories.author: Alexander Toshev
bullet_points: The research focuses on improving the performance of LLM agents designed to use external tools for complex, multi-step tasks.
A novel pipeline, SynthAPI, is introduced to control the diversity of synthetically generated tool-use training environments.
The study investigates how varying environment composition (tools, tasks, databases) impacts agent training effectiveness.

stories.title: GAS-PFN: Graph-Aware Spatiotemporal Prior-Data Fitted Networks for Zero-Shot Traffic Forecasting
stories.author: Rui Wu
bullet_points: Introduces GAS-PFN, a new model for zero-shot traffic forecasting that incorporates graph-aware spatiotemporal modeling.
Addresses the limitation of traditional supervised models by using Prior-Data Fitted Networks (PFNs) for deployment on new, unseen road networks.
The approach leverages synthetic task priors to encode domain-specific assumptions, enabling generalization without extensive retraining.

stories.title: Understanding the limits of latent world models
stories.author: Steffen Schneider
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in current world model evaluations, which often focus only on task performance.
It introduces the concept of 'faithful latent world models' to assess if learned models capture the true underlying environmental structure.
Faithfulness is defined via an equivariance condition between the environment's transition map and the learned latent dynamics.

stories.title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
stories.author: Amir Gholami
bullet_points: Addresses limitations in current reflective prompt optimizers (like GEPA) used in LLM agents.
Argues that not all agentic failures provide useful learning signals, as they can stem from prompt weaknesses or execution noise.
Proposes a solution, GEPA-Curator, to curate which tasks are provided to agents to ensure meaningful learning.

stories.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
stories.author: Ying-Cong Chen
bullet_points: Investigates the potential of Large Language Models (LLMs) to discover unknown or altered physical laws.
Proposes 'LongChang,' an automated framework for simulating worlds with modified physics.
Tests if LLMs can autonomously identify anomalies and derive underlying physical rules without explicit guidance.

stories.title: Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing
stories.author: Zhiwei Deng
bullet_points: Addresses the quadratic time complexity limitation of standard self-attention in LLMs.
Proposes Multi-State Linear Attention (MSLA) to improve efficiency by segmenting and compressing context.
Introduces 'Generalized Second-Order Routing' to aggregate information from memory states using mean alignment.

stories.title: Metacognitive Decoding: Efficient Inference for Diffusion Language Agents
stories.author: Dimitris N. Metaxas
bullet_points: Introduces a 'metacognitive controller' to guide diffusion language model generation.
The controller optimizes computation by learning when to finalize tokens and how far to generate.
Aims to make diffusion language agents more efficient for real-world interaction.

stories.title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions
stories.author: Khalil El Khammar
bullet_points: The paper investigates how memory compression affects the decision-making process of LLM groups.
It proposes two heuristics for memory retention: keeping the rarest claims or claims relevant to decision criteria.
A new diagnostic benchmark, CrossProfile, is introduced to test these memory failure modes.

stories.title: Teach reality, not ethics: a drop-in continued-pretraining corpus installs coupled human-biosphere-AI welfare dispositions across model families
stories.author: Mingxun Wang
bullet_points: The research addresses the gap in LLM training regarding ecological reasoning and the potential for models to cause irreversible harm to living systems.
A new 'coupled welfare' corpus is introduced, which integrates real-world data on human-biosphere-AI dependency and the value of irreversibility.
The corpus is designed for continued pre-training to instill specific welfare dispositions across various LLM families.

stories.title: Survival LLM: AI assistant and emergency library that runs on your own computer
stories.author: Luc
bullet_points: Introduction of 'Survival LLM,' an AI assistant designed for local, on-device operation.
The key feature is its ability to function as an emergency library, implying offline capability.
This addresses concerns regarding data privacy and reliance on cloud-based AI services.

stories.title: Apple's git still trusts the compromised eMudhra certificates
stories.author: emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com by galadran
bullet_points: Apple's Git infrastructure is reportedly still trusting compromised eMudhra certificates.
This suggests a potential vulnerability or outdated trust mechanism within Apple's development tools.
The issue relates to certificate validation and security practices within the software supply chain.

stories.title: EU GenAI4EU Moves Into Execution With Nexus Hub and Public Sector Pilots
stories.author: alifar
bullet_points: The EU's GenAI4EU initiative is transitioning from planning/funding to active implementation.
The execution phase involves the establishment of a 'Nexus Hub'.
The initiative is commencing practical application through public sector pilot projects.
